label: The speaker's ' would' or ''d' (subject I or we) right after an 'if you / if anyone ...' clause about something the reader might do, in a polite request or offer to the reader (the 'if you have X, I would appreciate it / we'd be happy to Y' closing); also the ' I' in 'correct me if I'm wrong / mistaken', and more weakly (about 0.3) phrasal 'come in' ('that's where X comes in', 'come in handy'). Quiet: 'would' after the speaker's own condition ('if I had money, I would...'), habitual or past 'would', 'would' with no 'if' clause, third-person subjects (he, they, my sister) in the same frame, and plain 'will be' / 'would have been'.
